learning: Iteration 4 showed sensor_size 0.016 at ±3 cm was the reference for this test. Still to learn: whether ±4 cm removes the remaining line loss without the s-bend penalty seen at 3 cm lead in iteration 2. rms_error near 0.03 on all tracks suggests a steady motor-mismatch offset, which is a gain question for later iterations.
notes: Package for the ±4 cm, 2 cm pitch, 16 mm test at 4 cm lead. Controller unchanged from iteration 4 (kp 3.0, kd 0.1, ki 0), so the geometry is the only variable. Weights x/0.02 give [-2,-1,0,1,2], matching the proven ordering.
rationale: Iteration 4 (±3 cm span, 4 cm lead, 12 mm footprints) was the best reference, with s-bend progress 0.155, oval 0.11 and one line loss per run. Iteration 2 (±6 cm, 3 cm lead) removed line losses but collapsed s-bend progress to 0.04. Iteration 3 (2 cm lead) also collapsed s-bend progress to 0.04. The 3 cm lead and the wide span were confounded in iteration 2, so the ±4 cm span at 4 cm lead is still untested. I keep the Builder's geometry as proposed: five sensors at x = -0.04 to +0.04 in 2 cm steps, y = 0.04 m, 16 mm footprints, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius, 0.18 x 0.12 m body. Weights are [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], which equal x/0.02. This is the same signal ordering and per-sensor weight pattern that worked in iteration 4, so the controller needs no rescaling. Gains stay at kp 3.0, ki 0, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.6 and line_loss 'last_direction', so the Builder's single-variable test is preserved. rms_error stays near 0.03 on all tracks in every iteration, which points to a motor-mismatch offset. I do not add ki here because the test is geometry-only and integral action on a curved course is untested. Expected result, not measured: line_loss_events falls toward 0 with progress at or above 0.155 on the s-bend. If the oval falls below 0.11, the span is too wide.
